gap: No result ChatGPT got states that CyberPower's pure-sine CP850PFCLCD ($169.95 on Amazon, 2026-11-17) costs only $5 more than ChatGPT's own middle pick, the CP850AVRLCD ($164.95 at Cable Plus USA, 2026-11-17), which switches to a simulated sine wave on battery, or that UGREEN's DC NAS UPS units cost $69.99 (US2000) and $109.99 (US3000) at UGREEN's store today.
standout_why: I compared against holdbackup.com (cited), racksandwatts.com and techfromalex.com. holdbackup and racksandwatts give no prices at all and only say 'Check price on Amazon'. techfromalex puts the CP850PFCLCD in a '$100–200' band and the BE600M1 in a '$50–100' band, with no dates and no exact figures, and it never mentions the CP850AVRLCD. None of the three names a DC UPS or any UGREEN UPS. The Synology compatibility lists and KB pages ChatGPT cited give no prices or waveforms. ChatGPT itself showed $164.95 and $169.95 but did not say that the cheaper card is simulated sine.
decides: Among ChatGPT's three AC picks, the CP850AVRLCD loses: for $5 less you get a simulated-sine unit, and NAS power supplies with active PFC can misbehave on simulated sine (techfromalex's point). That makes the CP850PFCLCD the AC pick for a 2–4-bay Synology, QNAP or TrueNAS box. For UGREEN NASync owners, the US2000 at $69.99 and the US3000 at $109.99 both undercut every AC pick ChatGPT priced, which supports our page's lead for that audience.
